candidate.answerReason: March has a price drop of $2.50, larger than the drops in January ($0.50), May ($1.50), and June ($2.00).

methods.label: Compare the monthly decreases
methods.explanation:
A monthly drop is the price at the beginning of the month minus the price at its end. We therefore compare the downward segments of the graph.

[Figure 1](figures/1993_AMC_8_Q10_question_fig1.svg)

The decreases, in dollars, are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{January: }&2.5-2.0=0.5,\\
\text{March: }&4.0-1.5=2.5,\\
\text{May: }&4.5-3.0=1.5,\\
\text{June: }&3.0-1.0=2.0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The price rises during February and April, so neither month has a drop. The greatest decrease is \(\$2.50\), during March. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
